summary: CCC stone overlook on Brian Head Peak, built 1934-35; wind tore off its roof in 2022; rebuilt and celebrated in September 2026.

facts.design: Stone observation building with a roof, built by CCC Camp F-16 in 1934-35

access.note: Public overlook with plaques inside, per the Forest Service; a hiking guide advises checking current access before travel

visit.trail_note: A short drive or walk reaches the building (Nevada Hiking); the 1934-35 road is still in place and accessible by sedan (Forest Service)

events.note: Built in 1934-35 by CCC Camp F-16 at Duck Creek; year given is the start of the work
Restored by Sierra Club volunteers in the 1990s; the Forest Service gives no single year
Wind tore the roof off in mid-November 2022
New structure completed on the summit; celebration reported in September 2026

notes_for_editor: Forest Fire Lookout Association's Utah list (cached) files Brian Head under Unknown/Undocumented Sites, while the Forest Service and KSL call it a fire lookout (the Forest Service says occasional). Story reports both. Elevation: KSL and Hoodline give 11,312 ft; Nevada Hiking says about 11,307 ft; story uses 11,312 ft from KSL. Record kind is unknown; the structure is a stone building, not a tower, so kind may need setting. No correction applied. Hoodline relies on KSL for most facts and adds the partner list; it says a local hiker found the damage while KSL says locals spotted the rubble, which does not change the story. KSL photo (Mike Saemisch) has no stated licence, so no photo was added. Two web searches used, within budget.
